title: OTLP-proxy design, log-shipping smoke tests, and Terraform test checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for OTLP proxy placement and log-shipping smoke tests for private deployments (VPC & on-prem). Intended audience: SREs, infra engineers preparing Terraform modules and upgrade cutovers, and solutions engineers validating customer installs.

Status/context notes (why this exists):
- Customers running Redwood Private often restrict egress and require an internal OTLP proxy that multiplexes traces/metrics/logs to our managed endpoints or to a customer remote write target.
- We need a repeatable test checklist and Terraform verification steps to safely roll out OTEL collector/OTLP-proxy changes and new log-shipping routes (fluent-bit -> kafka -> s3 or direct to syslog).
- This doc collects design constraints, Terraform test plan, and minimal smoke tests for cutover. It intentionally skews pragmatic (short failure modes + rollback) rather than exhaustive.

High-level design proposal (short):
- Deploy an OTLP-proxy service as a small fleet (2-3 replicas) inside the customer's observability namespace. Acts as a local relay with:
  - TLS termination for inbound OTLP/gRPC and HTTP/JSON (mutual TLS optional per customer)
  - Fanout rules: forward to (a) local Prometheus remote_write endpoint, (b) internal Kafka for logs, or (c) Redwood ingest over private peering (when enabled).
  - Rate-limiter with per-tenant token bucket (configurable via ConfigMap).
  - Health endpoints: /healthz, /ready and /metrics (Prom-compatible).

OTEL-collector vs lightweight proxy tradeoffs:
- Full OTEL collector: flexible processing, sampling, attribute rewriting; heavier memory/cpu. Recommended when customers need on-prem processing.
- Lightweight otlp-proxy (envoy + small adapter): very low overhead, stable routing, easier rolling upgrades. Use for high-throughput, low-transformation paths.

Terraform module notes (work-in-progress):
- Module: private_deployments/observability/otlp_proxy
  - Inputs to expose: replica_count, cpu_request, memory_request, backend_targets (list), mTLS_enabled (bool), kafka_config_id, remote_write_targets (list), namespace, service_account_annotations.
  - Outputs: service_dns, hpa_enabled (bool), otlp_proxy_config_map_name.
  - Acceptance check in module: create a smoke-testing job (k8s Job) that sends a small sample payload to the local proxy and checks /metrics for a 200 response. This job is created only when var.enable_smoke_test == true to avoid side effects in non-test runs.
  - Notes: avoid embedding credentials in module outputs; instead write a sealedsecret reference if needed.

Terraform testing checklist (pre-merge / CI / manual):
- Unit/plan checks: ensure all newly added variables have descriptions and defaults where appropriate. Run terraform validate + tflint.
- Integration sandbox test (short-lived cluster or k3s instance):
  1) Apply module with enable_smoke_test=true, kafka_config pointing to test-kafka.
  2) Verify Job completes successfully and returns curl 200 from within pod to service_dns:4317.
  3) Confirm /metrics contains otlp_proxy_up 1 and proxy_forward_success_total > 0.
- Upgrade path test:
  - Create v1 (simple config) then perform module upgrade to v2 with config changes (rate-limits lowered and new backend added). Validate zero-downtime by running continuous test traffic (see smoke tests below).

Smoke tests (minimal commands & expectations):
- From CI/test-pod inside cluster:
  - Test gRPC OTLP path:
    grpcurl -plaintext -d '{"resource_spans": []}' localhost:4317 opentelemetry.proto.collector.trace.v1.TraceService/Export
    Expect: HTTP/2 200 or success envelope.
  - Test metrics endpoint: curl -sf http://localhost:9100/metrics | grep otlp_proxy_up
    Expect: value 1 within 30s of startup.
  - Test logs path (fluent-bit -> proxy -> kafka):
    - Send a single JSON line to the fluent-bit tail input mounted in test pod.
    - Validate the message appears in the test Kafka topic (use kafkacat or kafka-console-consumer) within 20s.

Failure modes and quick mitigations: (keep short)
- TLS handshake failures: check serviceAccount certificate mount, ensure CA bundle mounted to proxy, verify mTLS toggle in config map. Quick mitigation: flip proxy to accept plaintext (only in isolated test envs) and re-run smoke test to confirm routing.
- Rate-limiter tripping unexpectedly: set token_bucket to generously high values in test config and observe behavior. If real traffic suppressed, scale replica_count up.
- Kafka auth issues: confirm SASL/SSL creds in sealedsecret, and that proxy pod can resolve and reach kafka brokers (nslookup + curl).

Cutover plan for on-prem customer (summary):
1) Pre-cutover: run integration test in customer staging cluster (same k8s version). Leave both current collector and new otlp-proxy running with proxy in passive mode (forward to a shadow topic).
2) Canary: route 5% of customer traffic through new proxy (use iptables or service mesh traffic split). Monitor latency, error rate, and drop counters for 24 hours.
3) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple hours if metrics stable.
4) Verification: ensure remote_write success metrics and that Prometheus scrape targets are still reachable.
5) Post-cutover: keep old collector running for 48 hours in read-only mode (no more forwarding) and only remove after logs/metrics reconciliation.

Rollback steps (fast):
- Flip traffic split to old collector (service selector change or traffic manager config).
- Scale otlp-proxy replicas to 0 and annotate pods with rollback reason.
- Open immediate incident (OBS-1427 style) and attach smoke test outputs.

Observability dashboards & alerts to watch during cutover:
- otlp_proxy_up (should be 1 for all replicas)
- proxy_forward_latency_ms (P95 < 200ms ideally internal)
- proxy_forward_error_rate (alerts if > 0.5% sustained over 5m)
- fluentbit_out_records_total (should match expected ingestion rate approx)
- kafka_lag_by_topic (any sudden jump indicates consumer issue)

Notes for solutions engineers validating customer installs:
- Always collect: pod logs for otlp-proxy, oc describe pod output, sealedsecret cypher metadata, and smoke test job logs.
- Keep copies of terraform plan outputs for the run that produced the change (store as artifact).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a central test harness that can connect to customer clusters and run smoke-tests automatically? (Pros: faster validation; Cons: requires cross-vpc connectivity).
- Define standard test payload sizes for latency benchmarking (small/medium/large traces and batch sizes).
- Finalize mTLS rotation cadence and secret management pattern in Terraform for sealedsecrets vs external KMS.

Reference quick links and useful commands:
- Confluence architecture draft: https://confluence.redwood/obs/otlp-proxy-arch-2024
- Jira epic: OBS-1427
- Quick local test pod: kubectl run obs-test --image=ghcr.io/redwood/tools:latest --restart=Never --command -- sleep 3600
- Collect logs: kubectl logs deploy/otlp-proxy -n observability --tail=200

Appendix (one-line checklist for reviewers):
- [ ] Terraform variables documented and secrets not leaked
- [ ] Smoke-test job passes in sandbox
- [ ] Canary traffic split configured and test traffic running
- [ ] Alerting dashboards created and verified
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated in practice run

End of draft. Add notes/inline comments here as you run tests.
